content:
## T1021.001 - Remote Services - Remote Desktop Protocol

This entry covers an adversary behaviour observed in intrusions against provider organisations. Adversaries use remote desktop sessions to move between systems, an approach that blends into healthcare estates where clinical support staff use the same mechanism routinely.

**Tactic:** Lateral Movement

**Platforms:** Windows

## Healthcare context

Clinical engineering and application support teams use remote desktop constantly, which makes volume-based detection unworkable and forces reliance on relationship-based detection.

## Detection

Sessions between host pairs with no prior history; sessions from clinical workstations to server infrastructure; session chains traversing three or more hosts.

## Mitigations

- Restrict remote desktop initiation to designated administrative hosts.
- Require multi-factor authentication for administrative sessions.
- Alert on host-pair combinations not seen in an established baseline.

## Notes for defenders

- Legitimate volume is high, so novelty of the host pair is a better signal than the session count.
- Session chaining across three or more hosts has almost no legitimate equivalent in normal support work.
- Restricting initiation to administrative hosts is more tractable than restricting destinations.
